newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan bourse ends week 2.4 percent higher.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan bourse ends week 2.4 percent higher.

text.p: The Casablanca stock market closed on Friday 2.4 percent higher from last week with leading stocks consolidating gains, a stockbroker said.
The all-share index closed at 530.05 points from 517.54 points last Friday.
ONA group the first biggest private holding closed at 675 dirhams, up 35 dirhams over a week.
Forecasts say that ONA net earnings are expected to reach 852 million dirhams ($92.6 million) in 1996 from 602 million dirhams in 1995.
Societe Nationale d'Investissement, Morocco's second largest conglomerate which holds diversified stakes in more than 40 firms, rose five dirhams to 615 dirhams. It was up 19 dirhams during the week.
The conglomerate has a market capitalisation of more than 5.6 billion dirhams.
Banque Marocaine pour le Commerce et l'Industrie shed eight dirhams to 420 dirhams, adding 27 dirhams from last Friday.
Leading stock Wafabank was up one dirham to 677 dirhams. It took two dirhams on the week.
Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur, a blue chip stock, edged up one dirham to trade at 471 dirhams, down four dirhams from the previous week.
Samir oil refinery, the country's main refinery, lost five dirhams to close at 265 dirhams. It dipped 14 dirhams since last Friday after one-week steady gains.
"Samir accounted for a large part of the trade with 22,027 shares exchanged on the official market," broker at ABN Amro Finance said.
Newly floated Credor slipped five dirhams to 600 dirhams. It lost 23 dirhams on the previous week.
Traded volume on the official market was 37.9 million dirhams from 99.9 million dirhams last Friday.
